newsitem.title: INDIA: ONE IN THREE INDIANS SEE NATION BREAKING APART.
newsitem.headline: ONE IN THREE INDIANS SEE NATION BREAKING APART.

text.p: One in three Indians believes the country will break apart into separate nations over the next five decades, according to a poll published ahead of the 50th anniversary of independence.

Thirty-six percent of the respondents in the poll published by India Today magazine said India would disintegrate into independent nations in the next 50 years, while 41 percent said it would stay united.
The survey, based on interviews with 12,651 adults by polling organisation ORG-MARG in May and June, showed Indira Gandhi, not Mahatma Gandhi, was regarded as the most inspiring leader.
Indira Gandhi, who ruled as prime minister for 15 years between 1966 and 1984, when she was assassinated, was named by 18 percent of the respondents as the most inspirational.
India's spiritual father Mahatma Gandhi, who was no relation to Indira, was chosen by 14 percent.

Indira Gandhi's father Jawaharlal Nehru, the first prime minister, was placed fourth with his grandson Rajiv Gandhi, behind Atal Bihari Vajpayee, a leader of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

The vast majority of the respondents -- 88 percent -- said they would choose to be reborn as an Indian. But only 29 percent said their quality of life had improved in the past five years, while nearly one quarter percent said it had deteriorated.
Corruption was named as the greatest evil by 34 percent, followed by unemployment with 20 percent and inflation with 18.
Forty-one percent said Indians are very corrupt. Fully half said police were dishonest while 46 percent said the same of politicians.

The poll revealed continued attachment to the socialist economy. There was more support for keeping state firms in the government's hands than in privatising them, and three quarters of the respondents said farm income should not be taxed.
Half said they feared Western culture would overpower India's, and nearly three quarters said they would not allow their son or daughter to marry someone from another caste.
Almost half predicted relations with Pakistan would never improve, and 71 percent said it was worth keeping Kashmir, the origin of two of the three wars between the neighbours.
India celebrates 50 years of independence on August 15.
